chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Ash'ari, from Samakah ibn Mihran, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah, the Exalted, did not send any Prophet or Imam except that he is the most knowledgeable of the people regarding Allah's affairs, the best in them, and the most perceptive of them.'
He said: 'And He did not make him except in a lineage from which they would recognize him and know him, so that they would know that they cannot disbelieve in him after knowing him.'

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah choose Prophets and Imams from specific lineages?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights how divine wisdom mandates that Prophets and Imams be chosen from recognized lineages, ensuring their authority is indisputable and preventing denial even after clear knowledge. This emphasis on known ancestry serves as a practical safeguard against sectarian confusion, anchoring the concept of *Nass* (designation) in tangible, historical reality. By linking recognition to lineage, the tradition ensures that the Imamate remains accessible and verifiable for the community.
